name: Stillings Hall
use: Former dining hall at 20 Ballard St; closed for dining since fall 2021; current use unconfirmed
architect: Alonzo J. Harriman Associates Inc. (contractor Davison Construction Co.)
statusNote: Closed as a dining hall since fall 2021; current use unconfirmed

facts.text: Designed by Alonzo J. Harriman Associates and built by Davison Construction; operational from December 1963 and dedicated May 9, 1964.
Named for Charles Edwin Stillings (class of 1900), a railroad power-plant foreman who saved and gave nearly a quarter-million dollars to UNH in 1960.
In August 2021 UNH delayed opening Stillings, one of three main Durham dining halls, because of the national labor shortage, moving staff to Holloway Commons and Philbrook.

s3.title: Stillings dining hall closed due to labor shortage (Sept 2021)

verdict: Harriman's 1963 dining pavilion with a scalloped-arch roofline, a mid-century gem standing idle since 2021.
notes: No 2022–2026 source found on reopening or reuse; status after 2021 is unconfirmed (it does not appear to operate as a dining hall). The 20 Ballard St address is from the old row and not re-verified. No review sources re-verified (old row's 2016 'quietest dining hall' claim not checked). Photo (TNH, ca. 2021): a striking mid-century modern pavilion: brick base, tall continuous glass walls and a scalloped roofline of shallow barrel vaults, which implies high, daylit dining rooms; ceilings/light inferred from the exterior only. No licensed photo found (searched the Commons category tree under 'University of New Hampshire' and 'Durham, New Hampshire', Commons file search by name, Commons geosearch at the building's coordinates, and Openverse/Flickr CC).
judgeNotes: Reference photos show a striking arched canopy roof. Exterior up two from the old run on that evidence.
